transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. To start, can you tell me what's been bringing you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you. Thanks for seeing me. Um, I'm here because... well, I guess I've always been a high-energy guy, which is usually a good thing, you know? Especially being a firefighter, it helps to be ready to go. But lately, I feel like I'm just always running hot, like I can't shut the motor off. I don't want to make it sound like a huge deal, but it's been causing some friction at the firehouse, and I just want to make sure I'm doing everything right. Does that make sense?
When you say you've been 'running hot' lately, is this a noticeable shift from how you normally feel, or is it more how you've felt for as long as you can remember?

Well, to be honest... it's probably not a new shift. I mean, I've always been pretty active. Actually, my mom likes to remind me that I was kind of like this way back in grade school, too. Not in a bad way, really! Just... you know, a typical energetic boy. 

She says I was always popping out of my seat, or maybe blurting out answers a bit too quickly. And I guess I misplaced my homework here and there, which meant some notes got sent home. But she always makes sure to say I was bright enough to do the work, you know? I just had a lot of spirit, I guess. 

So, yeah, I suppose it's been how I've felt for as long as I can remember. I hope I'm explaining that right? I just don't want you to think I was a bad kid or a troublemaker or anything, just... enthusiastic. Is that the kind of information you're looking for?

Does this 'running hot' feeling stay pretty much the same all the time, or do you notice it comes in waves—like periods of feeling unusually elevated or restless followed by stretches of feeling low or slowed down?

No, no, it's not really like waves or anything like that. I definitely don't have periods where I feel... low, or slowed down. I'm a pretty positive guy, you know? I like to keep things moving. 

It's more just a constant... hum, I guess? Like I'm always ready to go, which, again, is usually great for the job. It's just that sometimes the motor stays on even when I'm supposed to be relaxing at the station between calls. But I don't have those big ups and downs you're talking about. I'm pretty steady, just... steady at a slightly higher speed. Does that make sense? I hope I'm answering that right.
Outside of work, do you notice this same restlessness or trouble focusing affecting things like your home life, relationships, or hobbies?

Well... um, I guess my wife might say it bleeds over a little bit. I really try to be present for them, I promise I do! But, yeah, even on my days off, I have a little bit of a hard time doing, you know, the quiet stuff with my family. 

Like if we're trying to just sit and watch a movie or relax, I... I usually end up getting up before I've been sitting for very long. I don't mean to be disruptive at all! I just start talking, or moving around, or I'll figure I should go check the tools in the garage and make sure everything is organized. I just like being productive for the house, you know? But I suppose it can be a little much for them when I can't just sit still and relax. 

I really hope that doesn't make me sound like a bad husband or father or anything. I just like to keep busy and make sure things are taken care of. Is that the kind of thing you were asking about?
Do you often find yourself losing track of details, forgetting things, or having trouble staying focused on tasks—whether at work or at home—separate from the restlessness you've described?

Well... um, I guess maybe a little bit? But mostly just with the paperwork side of things! Out in the field on a call, I'm completely locked in, I promise. 

It's just... well, sometimes I'll finish an incident report back at the station, and I'll think it's totally solid, you know? I really do try to be thorough. But then the captain will pull me aside and point out that I, um, maybe put the wrong unit number down, or missed a time stamp somewhere. Or sometimes I'll accidentally skip one of those little boxes that matters for the safety review. 

It's never anything intentional, and I always fix it right away as soon as he points it out! I just... I guess my brain moves a little faster than my pen sometimes, and I gloss over the tiny details. I really hope that doesn't make me sound careless or incompetent. I take the job incredibly seriously, I just struggle a bit with the forms. Does that answer your question okay?
Outside of the paperwork issues, do you often find yourself losing things like your keys or phone, forgetting appointments, or getting easily distracted when someone is talking to you?

Oh, um... well, I wouldn't say I'm losing my keys or anything major like that. I really try to stay organized, I do! But... I guess I do have a bit of a habit of forgetting things I genuinely mean to get done. 

Like, it's just little things, mostly. Sometimes I'll forget to sign off on the online training modules until the very last second, or I'll mean to call someone back and just... completely lose track of it. And, um, occasionally I might miss paying a bill until right before—or I guess sometimes right after—the late fee hits. Or I'll show up for a shift and realize I forgot to bring the right gear paperwork in. 

I always feel terrible about it, and I really don't mean to be irresponsible! I always get it sorted out eventually. It's just... I get busy, and things slip my mind. I try my best to keep up with it all, I promise. Is that... is that normal for someone with a schedule like mine? I hope I'm not making myself sound completely unreliable.
